jobs.title: In-House CRA ( Australia)
jobs.description: Alimentiv is a global CRO with a singular focus: advancing therapies for patients with gastrointestinal diseases. GI is our WHY and for more than 30 years that purpose has driven our scientific rigour, operational excellence, and deep therapeutic expertise, including supporting more than 70% of IBD compounds in development. We operate as a private, profit-with-purpose company, channeling our commercial success back into scientific research, technology, and our people. With approximately 700 people across multiple countries and three service lines, we are growing deliberately, and the capability of our leaders and our organization is central to how we get there. If you want to do meaningful work, build something real, and invest back in research that changes lives — we want to meet you! Job Overview The In-House Clinical Research Associate (IHCRA) supports clinical site monitoring and management activities for clinical studies, ensuring compliance with study protocols, Alimentiv and sponsor procedures, ICH-GCP guidelines and applicable regulatory requirements. Acting as a key point of contact for investigative sites and internal project teams, the IHCRA plays an important role in supporting site performance, patient recruitment, data quality and study delivery. This role focuses primarily on remote site management, data review, query resolution and essential document collection, while working closely with field CRAs and Clinical Operations Leads (COLs) to ensure studies are conducted efficiently and in accordance with project requirements. Key Responsibilities Act as the primary in-house point of contact for assigned investigative sites, managing day-to-day communications, documenting site contacts and following up on outstanding actions and issues. Support remote site management activities, ensuring compliance with study protocols, visit schedules, data entry timelines and applicable regulatory requirements. Perform remote data review and analysis using EDC systems

jobs.title: Director, Enhanced Care Management
jobs.description: Join the dynamic journey at Vynca , where we're passionate about transforming care for individuals with complex needs. We’re more than just a team; we're a close-knit community. Our shared commitment to caring for each other and those we serve is what sets us apart. Guided by our unwavering core values: Excellence, Compassion, Curiosity, and Integrity, we forge paths of success together. Join us in this transformative movement where you can contribute to making a profound difference every day. At Vynca, our mission is to provide comprehensive care for more quality days at home. About the job The Director of Enhanced Care Management is responsible for directing and overseeing operations of the enhanced care management program. This includes responsibility for Cal AIM program performance, provider and community collaboration/engagement, oversight of the care management specialists, policy development, process improvement/program enhancements, managing interdependencies and risks, and developing growth opportunities. The director works on projects from the point of conceptualization up to the implementation stages, and is responsible for resolving complex problems. The director supports the VP of Clinical Operations in the development of strategy that results in better health quality outcomes, better patient care, and lower cost of care. The Director of Enhanced Care Management will develop, implement, supervise, and manage Vynca’s Enhanced Case Management Program. They will supervise Clinical Managers, Clinical Consultants and Lead Care Managers. This individual will be responsible for administering the ECM program, developing linkage with healthcare plans, outreach, creating clear and easy access and entry into the ECM program, program evaluation, and staff supervision. At this time we are only considering applicants in the following states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Illinois, Nevada, Oregon, Texas, Utah, and Washington. jobs.title: Lab Automation Lead
jobs.description: About us, and our mission At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platforms with a large cohort of patient-derived tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical outcomes, validate therapies and uncover new drug candidates. By generating multimodal, real-world data, we aim to make drug development smarter, faster and more personalized. We collaborate with leading hospitals, research institutes and pharmaceutical companies. Backed by leading investors, Orakl is a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of biology, automation and AI. Position overview Orakl runs a high-throughput 3D cell‑culture platform to culture patient-derived organoids (PDOs). These patient-derived specimens reveal critical information into the patient disease, but require heavy maintenance work. Automating these workflows will be critical to improve the reliability and traceability of experimental work. We are hiring our first automation lead to build the Automation function from scratch. This is a high ownership and high autonomy job. You will map our processes, decide what to automate and what to leave alone, specify and source the equipment, negotiate with vendors and integrators, commission the machines, run them with the lab team, and hire the people the function needs. As the ideal candidate, you have already put automated lines or special machines into service, and you know what typically breaks between commissioning and the first experimental runs. While previous experience in biology is a plus, it is not a strict requirement: you will be taught all you need to know. jobs.description: Â POSITION SUMMARY: Job Function: Clinical Operations Title: Senior Clinical Trial Systems Lead The Senior Clinical Trials Systems Lead serves as the business owner representative for Clinical Operations systems, such as CTMS and eTMF. This role defines business problems and intended use, facilitates the prioritization for system updates and enhancements, coordinates handoff to IT and product partners, reviews designs and prototypes iteratively, and coordinates user acceptance testing and go-live approval. This individual will work in partnership with IS&T, Product, UI/UX, QA, Training, and the vendors who design, build, and validate outsourced systems. The role is also the day-to-day business point of contact for users and cross-functional teams, supporting troubleshooting, and continuous system improvements. The Senior Clinical Trials Systems Lead helps ensure that systems meet the requirements of study protocols, regulatory standards, business objectives, and user needs, and are fit for their intended use. Â PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Partner directly with clinical science, quality, and regulatory teams to plan, test, and deploy new clinical systems and enhancements. Support system compliance with FDA, EMA, and ICH-GCP standards by defining GxP impact for all changes. Work closely with IS&T, QA, and product teams to manage system integrations, upgrades, and vendor service levels. Document stakeholder requirements clearly, identify process gaps, and propose actionable solutions. Review system designs and prototypes iteratively, providing fast, direct feedback. Coordinate and execute user acceptance testing (UAT), documenting results to provide final business sign-off. Serve as the primary functional support contact for internal teams, troubleshooting issues and escalating technical blockers to IS&T. jobs.title: Sr. Engineering Manager
jobs.description: About myTomorrows myTomorrows is a global health tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers for patients seeking treatment options. We strive to enable earlier and better treatment access by bridging the gap between those searching for possible options, and the companies who develop them. We work closely with patients, healthcare professionals, trial sites, patient advocacy groups, and BioPharma – connecting key stakeholders in the drug development ecosystem. We’ve developed a cutting-edge AI-powered technology platform that simplifies and streamlines access to drugs in development. To support our users and clients, we have a range of industry-expert specialized teams ready to help. Our services include clinical trial patient recruitment, Expanded Access Program management and Real-World Data collection. With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. In October 2025, we closed a €25M investment with Avego Healthcare Capital to fuel our global ambitions and scale the business. Join us in shaping the future of treatment access - making tomorrow’s therapies accessible for people who need them today. The Opportunity: Senior Engineering Manager As an Engineering Manager at myTomorrows, you will lead Backend, Frontend, Full Stack and QA engineers building the platforms that help patients find their treatment options. Our Expanded Access Program (EAP) platform and Clinical Trials (CT) platform connect patients and healthcare professionals with treatments in development and give our BioPharma Partners the tools to run their programs and trials. You’ll shape how these platforms grow, building a high-performing team that ships well-designed, scalable, secure and compliant software, and delivers it on time. You won’t do it alone.
